land.text: the Yellow River valley in Henan: 'Xie's descendant, Tang, overthrew Jie, the impious and cruel final Xia ruler in the Battle of Mingtiao'

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Xia dynasty; Predynastic Shang'. Cliopatria lacks the Xia; the ea-01-x additions batch writes it as a culture. The page gives no year for Mingtiao.

land.text: the Shang state after the 'Battle of Muye: c. 1046 BC'; King Wu 'allowed Di Xin's son Wu Geng to rule the Shang as a vassal kingdom', and the Shang house was later 'enfeoffed' as 'the Duke of Song'

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Shang to 1001 and starts the Zhou in 1000; the Zhou dossier adds a 1046 keyframe.

capitals.name: Bo (Yanshi or Zhengzhou)
capitals.note: Infobox capitals without years: 'Bo (either modern Yanshi or Zhengzhou)', 'Ao (near modern Zhengzhou)', 'Yan (near modern Qufu)', 'Xiang (near modern Anyang)'; 'the establishment of the dynasty with the foundation of an Erligang culture walled city at Yanshi'; 'the earth walls at Zhengzhou, erected in the 15th century BC'. One dot at Zhengzhou (gazetteer place) stands for the undated early capitals until Yin.

capitals.name: Yin (Yinxu, Anyang)
capitals.note: 'Yin served as the capital during the Late Shang period (c. 1250 – c. 1046 BCE)'; 'Pan Geng moved the capital from Yān' (undated); coordinates from the Yinxu infobox (36°07′21″N 114°19′07″E). The Shang page also lists 'Zhaoge (near modern Qi County, Hebi)' as a late seat.

keyframe_review.note: 154,175 km2 for 1600-1241 (Henan, southern Hebei, western Shandong, south-eastern Shanxi): the Erligang and Zhengzhou phases ('earth walls at Zhengzhou, erected in the 15th century BC'). Area check: the infobox gives 1,250,000 km2 for c. 1122 BC, 8.1 times Cliopatria; the page's own words are 'ruled in the Yellow River valley' and 'ruled over much of northern China', and the Erligang culture 'found across a wide area of China, even as far northeast as the area of modern Beijing' with 'Panlongcheng ... in the middle Yangtze valley' as 'an important regional centre'. The infobox figure counts the cultural sphere; the Cliopatria core is kept, and the outposts (Panlongcheng, the Beijing area) are not drawn as Shang territory. Soft edge.

The same 154,175 km2 for 1240-1101: the Anyang phase, 'Yin served as the capital during the Late Shang period (c. 1250 – c. 1046 BCE)'; 'The oldest extant direct records date from c. 1250 BC at the Yinxu site near Anyang' (Shang page). No page dates a border change; the only move is the capital (ledger, 1250).

correction.text: the shape as drawn, valid 1100 to 1046 BC only ('Battle of Muye: c. 1046 BC'); years only

keyframe_review.note: The same shape for 1100-1001, but the dynasty ended with the 'Battle of Muye: c. 1046 BC' ('argue for an end date of 1045 BC'; 'At least 44 dates for the end of the dynasty have been proposed, ranging from 1130 to 1018 BC'). The years 1045-1001 belong to the Zhou (that dossier's new 1046 keyframe).

region.text: the Yellow River valley in Henan; the Erligang walled cities at Yanshi and Zhengzhou

ledger.note: c. 1600: Tang of Shang founds the dynasty. Infobox 'Established: c. 1600 BC'; the dynasty's establishment identified 'with the foundation of an Erligang culture walled city at Yanshi'; Tang 'overthrew Jie, the impious and cruel final Xia ruler in the Battle of Mingtiao' (undated). The core is Cliopatria's shape; the page gives the Yellow River valley in Henan, not a boundary.

c. 1250: the capital at Yin (Anyang). 'Yin served as the capital during the Late Shang period (c. 1250 – c. 1046 BCE)', 'the reigns of 12 Shang kings'; the move under Pan Geng ('Pan Geng moved the capital from Yān') is undated on both pages, so the Late Shang period's start is used.

region.text: the Shang state, 'much of northern China' in the Yellow River valley

ledger.note: c. 1046: King Wu of Zhou wins at Muye; the Shang fall. Infobox 'Battle of Muye: c. 1046 BC'; Di Xin 'is said to have committed suicide after his army was defeated by Wu of Zhou'; Nivison and Shaughnessy 'argue for an end date of 1045 BC'. Wu Geng ruled 'the Shang as a vassal kingdom' and Weiziqi was enfeoffed 'as the Duke of Song' (Song's rites 'until Qi conquered Song in 286 BC'). Cliopatria keeps the Shang to 1001.

wars.name: Battle of Muye

zones.text: Muye, before the late Shang seat 'Zhaoge (near modern Qi County, Hebi)'

wars.outcome: Zhou victory: 'defeated Di Xin at the Battle of Muye, marking the beginning of the Zhou dynasty' (Zhou page); the Shang end c. 1046 (1045 for Nivison and Shaughnessy).
wars.note: The Shang page also records 'prolonged conflicts with northern frontier tribes called the Guifang' (undated) and the Battle of Mingtiao against the Xia (undated); neither is listed as a war for want of a year.

certainty.note: A Bronze Age state known from archaeology and oracle bones: every edge is approximate; the Erligang outposts (Panlongcheng on the middle Yangtze, the Beijing area) are a cultural sphere, not territory.

notes: Cliopatria rows to correct: the Shang end 1001 should be 1046 (the Zhou dossier adds a 1046-1001 keyframe). Area: the infobox's 1,250,000 km2 (c. 1122 BC) is 8.1 times Cliopatria's 154,175 km2; the researcher kept Cliopatria's core and treats the infobox figure as the cultural sphere (Erligang finds 'as far northeast as the area of modern Beijing', Panlongcheng on the middle Yangtze); the reviewer may prefer an adjust that adds the Panlongcheng outpost for the Erligang phase (1600-1400). Rulers: the king list is documented but only Wu Ding (c. 1250-1191) and Di Xin (c. 1075-1046) carry absolute dates on the page (the oracle-bone phases give overlapping ranges), so no ruler strip is written; a gap-filler can take the Xia–Shang–Zhou Chronology Project dates from 'List of rulers of China'. Predecessor: the Xia (xia-dynasty) needs the ea-01-x culture dossier; the Battle of Mingtiao is undated. Capitals before Yin (Bo, Ao, Yan, Xiang) have no years on the page; one dot at Zhengzhou stands for them.
